policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 28 Jan close (1x4 3.76, 3x6 3.48, 6x9 3.37, 9x12 3.35 vs WIBOR 3M 3.90) price roughly 55bp of NBP cuts within 12 months. The MPC held at 4.00% on 14 Jan. Glapiński (15 Jan): a terminal rate of about 3.5% with a real rate of at least 1-1.5%, cuts in 25bp steps; he excluded neither February nor March (or even April). Erste (23 Jan): the data significantly weaken the case for an early-February cut; it expects March and May. Duda (23 Jan): both February and March cuts look likely. NBP board member Sobon (28 Jan): room for further cuts, month by month; Pekao (28 Jan) sees 3.25% possible.
policy.risk_text: Strong December wages and industry cut the odds of a February move; the March projection is the gate. A hawkish projection (fiscal impulse ~7% of GDP deficit, 8.6% wages) would lift the front end; global long-end volatility and heavy supply weigh on the 10Y asset swap.

cpi.m: Dec final (GUS, 15 Jan); Nov 2.5%; Dec core 2.7% (NBP, 16 Jan)

macro.projection_text: NBP November 2025 projection: CPI 3.7% (2025), 2.9% (2026), 2.5% (2027); December 2025 CPI 2.4% y/y (final). The March 2026 projection is due with the March MPC meeting.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit ~7.0% of GDP; 2026 budget deficit cap PLN 271.7bn, gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn; FinMin Domański (16 Jan): the 2025 central-budget deficit came in a dozen-plus billion below the PLN 288.8bn limit; the President signed the 2026 budget on 19 Jan and referred it to the Constitutional Tribunal for follow-up review (the act is in force); Eurostat (22 Jan): general-government debt 58.1% of GDP at end-Q3 2025.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: Q1 2026 supply of PLN 75-100bn over 8 auctions; 2026 needs ~28% financed before the 28 Jan sale; a USD 10bn SEC shelf was filed on 20 Jan (published 21 Jan); Fitch (27 Feb) and Moody's (20 Mar) reviews with negative outlooks; Coface (20 Jan) flagged downgrade risk if the deficit path does not improve.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut six times in 2025 to 4.00% and held on 14 Jan; December CPI 2.4% y/y (final, 15 Jan), core 2.7%; the NBP projects 2.9% for 2026 (professional forecasters 2.6%); the March projection is the next policy gate. GDP grew 3.8% y/y in Q3; IMF (19 Jan) raised Poland's 2026 growth forecast to 3.5%. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 28 Jan: the last January auction sold PLN 12.0bn on 21.4bn demand (cover 1.78) plus 2.1bn additional; GPW Benchmark announced the 30 Jan index changes. The Fed held at 3.50-3.75% (10-2; Miran and Waller for a cut); Powell: policy near neutral, tariff-driven inflation; March cut odds ~12%; Brent ~$68.6.

calendar.plan_text: MoF Q1 2026 financing plan (31 Dec 2025): 8 sale auctions for PLN 75-100bn, one switch auction, possible foreign issuance; January sales 9 Jan (done: PLN 13.7bn incl. additional sale), 22 Jan (plan 8-13bn) and 28 Jan (7-12bn); EUR 3.25bn priced on 8 Jan. 16 Jan: 36-week T-bills PLN 3.8bn at 3.645%. MoF filed a USD 10bn shelf prospectus with the US SEC (20 Jan). 22 Jan result: PLN 12.0bn sold vs 17.1bn demand (cover 1.43) plus 1.75bn additional (NZ0331 1.04bn, WZ0930 0.59bn); stop yields OK0128 3.488%, PS0131 4.386%, DS0432 4.611%, DS1035 5.107%. MoF (26 Jan): ~28% of 2026 needs financed. 28 Jan result: PLN 12.0bn vs 21.4bn demand (cover 1.78) plus 2.11bn additional (DS1035 1.28bn, NZ0331 0.77bn); stop yields OK0128 3.529%, PS0131 4.392%, DS1034 4.970%, DS1035 5.093%. January wholesale sales ~PLN 41.6bn incl. additional sales.
calendar.timing_text: Within each auction week of the Aug 2025-Jan 2026 sample, yields drifted lower into the auction (rally regime) and the auction-day close was the cheapest point relative to the preceding session, so new buying is best executed at the auction-day close (the February dates (plan due 30 Jan)) rather than the day before. January auctions have been absorbed with cover of 1.4-1.9x, so supply is not the binding constraint. For the front end the 3-4 Feb MPC is the next event: strong December data pushed the consensus to a February hold; the March projection decides the cut timing.

facts.core_text: Regime: the NBP paused at 4.00% with ~55bp more priced, the ECB is done at 2.00% (a hike is the next move in market pricing), the Fed held on 28 Jan, the BoE eases gradually, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 56bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 227bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 28 Jan close). FOMC held with two dissents for a cut (28 Jan); UST 10Y ~4.25%.

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).

12 Jan BGK auction: PLN 3.73bn sold against 7.05bn demand, plus 0.71bn in the additional sale (~PLN 4.4bn, about a quarter of the 2026 FPC plan of up to 18.5bn); per-series levels were not found. The 1.9x cover shows real-money demand for guaranteed paper at these spreads.
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
